title: Rodri Pushes for Real Madrid Move as Florentino Pérez Holds the Key
excerpt: The 2026 World Cup Golden Ball winner has reached outline personal terms with Real Madrid, but Florentino Pérez must approve any deal with Manchester City.
body:
• Rodri is actively pushing for a transfer to Real Madrid after winning the 2026 World Cup Golden Ball with Spain
  • Real Madrid and Rodri are close to agreement on personal terms, according to journalist Matteo Moretto
  • Florentino Pérez has shifted from blocking the deal to being "much more open," though no formal talks with Manchester City have begun
  • Manchester City have offered Rodri a new contract, but his current deal expires in 2027 and he could leave as a free agent

Rodrigo Hernández's move to Real Madrid is gathering momentum after the Spain captain's starring role in the 2026 World Cup, with reports indicating the two parties have reached near-agreement on personal terms — but the transfer hinges on one man: Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano, Rodri is "doing everything possible" to make a return to Spain happen this summer. The 30-year-old midfielder, who was named the tournament's best player after leading La Roja to their second World Cup title, views a switch to the Santiago Bernabéu as a career ambition.

Personal Terms Close, but No Club-to-Club Talks

Journalist Matteo Moretto reported that Real Madrid already have Rodri's approval for a move and are described as "very close" to an agreement in principle on personal terms. The most significant shift, Moretto noted, is in Pérez's own stance — now characterized as "much more open" to signing the Manchester City midfielder.

https://x.com/Nawas_masood/status/2080039657023348802

That represents a direct contrast to the institutional resistance Real Madrid had been communicating in the weeks before the World Cup final. Just days ago, Romano reported that Pérez was personally "blocking" any pursuit of Rodri, despite the player's well-known desire to wear the famous white shirt.

"I can guarantee that Rodri dreams of Real Madrid, but right now there is a new contract proposal on the table from Man City."

— Fabrizio Romano, transfer journalist

However, the shift in Real Madrid's internal position has not yet translated into formal contact with Manchester City. No negotiations are underway between the two clubs, leaving a significant gap between where the situation stands and where it would need to be for a deal to materialize.

Manchester City's Counter-Move

City are not sitting idle. The club have presented Rodri with a substantial new contract offer, which Romano described as "a very important offer financially for a 30-year-old player." His current deal runs until the summer of 2027, meaning City face the prospect of losing one of their greatest-ever signings for nothing if he declines to extend.

Hugo Viana, City's director of football who replaced Txiki Begiristain last year, holds the decisive card on whether the club would even entertain offers — and at what price. City signed Rodri from Atlético Madrid for a then-club-record £62.8 million in 2019, and he has been central to the club's domestic and European dominance since.

If Rodri departs, City would likely accelerate their pursuit of Lille's highly-rated Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi, who has been linked with an £85 million move. Enzo Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager, would also have the experienced Nico González, Tijjani Reijnders, and Mateo Kovačić as midfield alternatives — though none have replicated Rodri's influence.

The World Cup Factor

Rodri's performances in the United States cemented his status as one of the premier midfielders of his generation. He was awarded the Golden Ball — joining an elite group of World Cup legends — after orchestrating Spain's run to the title under Luis de la Fuente.

That recognition appears to have been the tipping point for Pérez. The Real Madrid president had previously been unconvinced about pursuing a 30-year-old, especially given the financial outlay required. But the combination of World Cup triumph, Golden Ball recognition, and a contract entering its final year seems to have produced the shift in stance that Moretto's report describes.

Rodri himself hinted at his openness to a move in March, telling reporters: "You cannot turn down the best clubs in the world." He added that his time at Atlético Madrid — where he came through the youth system — would not prevent him from playing for their city rivals Real.

What Happens Next

The ball is now in Pérez's court. If the Real Madrid president greenlights a formal approach, City would demand a fee commensurate with Rodri's stature — likely well in excess of the £62.8 million they paid seven years ago, even with just one year left on his contract. Alternatively, Rodri could accept City's contract offer and postpone his Bernabéu dream by at least another season, potentially leaving as a free agent in 2027.

For now, Romano's assessment captures the state of play: Rodri's desire is clear, Real Madrid's resistance is softening, but the decisive phone call between the two clubs has yet to be made.
